content: 1. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Similarly, clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lopinavir through the same mechanism. Both drugs also prolong the QTc interval, which can increase the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 2. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of loratadine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additionally, clarithromycin increases loratadine levels via the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown, but caution is advised. 3. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while clarithromycin increases lorlatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lorlatinib dose by 25 mg/day. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, return to the previous lorlatinib dose after three plasma half-lives of the inhibitor. 4. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of lovastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. This interaction is contraindicated due to the increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. 5. Clarithromycin increases the levels of lumacaftor/ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. However, due to the induction effect of lumacaftor on CYP3A4, the net exposure of ivacaftor is not expected to exceed levels seen with ivacaftor monotherapy. No dose adjustment is necessary when initiating CYP3A4 inhibitors in patients already on lumacaftor/ivacaftor. When starting lumacaftor/ivacaftor in patients on strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the dose to one tablet daily for the first week, then resume the recommended dose. 6. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the lumateperone dose to 5 mg/day. 7. Clarithromycin and lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Clarithromycin also increases lumefantrine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 8. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the potential for serious adverse reactions. 9. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of lurbinectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor for five half-lives, return to the previous lurbinectedin dose. 10. Clarithromycin and macimorelin both prolong the QTc interval. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 milliseconds in the corrected QT interval. Avoid coadministration with drugs that prolong the QT interval to reduce the risk of torsades de pointes. Allow sufficient washout time of QT-prolonging drugs before administering macimorelin. 11. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of macitentan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 12. Clarithromycin and maprotiline both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 13. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Decrease the maraviroc dose to 150 mg twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 14. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of marijuana by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Marijuana may also increase clarithromycin levels through the same mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 15. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure caused by systolic dysfunction. 16. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mavorixafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. Adjust the mavorixafor dose if needed. 17. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of medroxyprogesterone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 18. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of toxicity. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 19. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mestranol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. It may also decrease mestranol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and has a low risk of contraceptive failure. 20. Clarithromycin and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Clarithromycin also increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 21. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of methylergonovine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of serious adverse effects. 22. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitor closely for systemic corticosteroid side effects. 23. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of metronidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 24. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of miconazole (vaginal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 25. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of midazolam (oral and intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. 26. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of midostaurin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 27. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Do not exceed 300 mg/day of mifepristone for Cushing syndrome when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. This combination may also prolong the QT interval. Use alternatives if available. 28. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mirtazapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 29. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mirvetuximab soravtansine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase exposure to the cytotoxic component of the drug, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. Monitor closely. 30. Mitotane decreases clarithromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 31. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of modafinil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 32. Clarithromycin increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters, which increases plasma concentrations of momelotinib. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 33. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of mometasone (inhaled and intranasal) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This increases the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Monitor closely. 34. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 35. Clarithromycin and moxifloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 36. Clarithromycin decreases the effects of nafcillin due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic antibiotics like clarithromycin may interfere with the bactericidal actions of penicillins. 37. Clarithromycin increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitor for potential adverse effects if coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 38. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of naloxegol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 39. Clarithromycin decreases the levels of nateglinide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This may result in hypoglycemia; monitor glucose levels closely. 40. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of nefazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Nefazodone also increases clarithromycin levels through the same mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. 41. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Nelfinavir may also increase clarithromycin levels. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 42. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of neomycin (oral) by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 43. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of neratinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 44. Clarithromycin increases the levels or effects of netupitant/palonosetron by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Netupitant is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, but no dosage adjustment is required. 45. Clarithromycin significantly increases the levels or effects of nevirapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs.
